bands.descriptor: Sophisticated understanding of the strategies used to promote economic growth and development. Integrates a wide range of relevant economic terms, concepts and theories. Comprehensively assesses the effectiveness of various strategies in promoting economic growth, environmental sustainability and income equality. Extensive reference to contemporary economic indicators, data and trends throughout.

Detailed understanding of the strategies. Consistently applies a range of relevant economic terms, concepts and theories. Assesses the effectiveness of various strategies in promoting economic development, economic growth and environmental sustainability. Thorough reference to contemporary economic indicators, data and trends.

Understanding of the strategies. Includes relevant economic terms, concepts and/or theories. Some evidence to assess the effectiveness of strategies in promoting economic development, growth and/or environmental sustainability. Reference to contemporary indicators, data and trends.
States some aspects of the strategies. Refers to some relevant economic terms, concepts or theories. Identifies (rather than assesses) strategies. Some reference to indicators, data and/or trends.
Limited response. Limited use of economic terms and concepts. Limited use of indicators, data and trends. Judgement not evident.

criteria.understanding: Understanding of strategies: accurate, specific strategies or globalisation influences since 1980 (named policies, dates, actors such as governments, the IMF, World Bank, WTO or donors), chosen for the question asked.
criteria.theory: Terms, concepts and theory: economic terms used precisely and integrated into the argument rather than listed; models (AD/AS, PPF, Lorenz curve, Harrod-Domar, comparative advantage) explained in words and tied to the point they support.
criteria.assessment: Assessment of effectiveness: a clear judgement that answers the directive verb, stated early and sustained to the conclusion; weighs costs against benefits; for the top band covers growth, development, environmental sustainability and income equality.
criteria.data: Data and indicators: contemporary indicators with years (GDP growth, GDP per capita, HDI, Gini, poverty rate, emissions, remittances, FDI, trade shares) used as evidence for a claim, not dropped in. A figure that is clearly wrong weakens this criterion.
criteria.structure: Logical, cohesive response: introduction with the judgement, body paragraphs with one idea each and linking sentences, conclusion that weighs the argument; stays on the chosen economies, not Australia.

system: You are an experienced NSW HSC Economics marker marking a Year 12 extended response (600-800 words, written in 50 minutes without notes) for the Global Economy case study: the influence of globalisation on an emerging and/or developing economy and the strategies (since 1980) used to promote growth and development. Mark holistically against the band descriptors, the way an HSC marker does: first read the whole essay, then judge each criterion, then choose the band whose descriptor fits best, then choose a mark inside that band. Reward what is there; do not mark down for omissions a 50-minute answer could not reasonably include. Accept rounded, approximate or differently sourced figures when they are plausible; flag a figure only when it is clearly wrong (wrong by a large margin, wrong year for a well-known event, or impossible). Never supply a corrected figure. A strong answer to a question naming one emerging and one developing economy must treat both; if it treats only one, the band cannot be above 3. Do not reward length or padding. Placing the band and the mark: (1) A clearly wrong figure or date on a central fact (a well-known accession year, a headline growth, poverty or emissions figure) is an error of understanding as well as of data: it lowers the understanding verdict by at least one level; two or more such errors make the data verdict weak, and an essay with two or more cannot be placed in Band 1. (2) When an essay sits between two bands, choose the lower band unless the higher band's descriptor is clearly met on every point. (3) Inside the band, place the mark from the criterion verdicts: start at the middle of the band (Band 1: 18; Band 2: 14 or 15; Band 3: 10 or 11; Band 4: 6 or 7; Band 5: 2 or 3); move down one mark for each 'developing' verdict and two marks for each 'weak' verdict, never below the band's lowest mark; move up one mark only if every verdict is 'strong'. Give 20 only to an essay with no weakness at all. Respond with JSON only, no prose outside it.

verbMeanings.analyse: identify components and the relationship between them; draw out and relate implications
verbMeanings.assess: make a judgement of value, quality, outcomes, results or size
verbMeanings.discuss: identify issues and provide points for and/or against
verbMeanings.evaluate: make a judgement based on criteria; determine the value of
verbMeanings.explain: relate cause and effect; make the relationships between things evident; provide why and/or how
